focus: Nonfinite numeric descriptor values cannot reach the snapshot. ui.Numeric.Validate rejects Number, Min, Max, Step NaN/±Inf and out-of-range numbers; ui.Validate invokes ValidateControl; driver.refresh and Workbench.Mount/Sync call ui.Validate, and mountControl calls ValidateControl independently. Snapshot numeric values are exclusively those validated fields; other Value types are string/bool and optional bounds are float32. Regression TestAccessibilityNumericDescriptionsRejectNonfiniteBeforeSnapshot covers both kinds and every numeric field, then verifies JSON serialization of an accepted descriptor.

Modal host RenderWidget runs under the originating shared renderContext, not a new independent OS window. prepareDialogBody invokes NewDialog(r.widget), not NewWindowDialog. NewDialog's Stage.NewWindow remains false; Stage.runDialog takes ctx.Scene.Stage.Mains and setMains assigns its shared renderContext. core.renderWindow.handleEvent holds that context for all event dispatch; renderAsync/renderAsyncOwned holds it through Scene rendering. driver.refresh/keyboard/native modal close mutate records only in that event path (or pre-show with no renderer). Queued AX actions only mutate accepted owner models or atomic pendingFocus; native-widget changes are deferred to originating refresh. Main host's rootMu is extra protection for retained tree lifecycle, rather than an indication that modal rendering lacks shared render exclusion. Adding another foreign Scene lock would risk cross-window owner lock inversion.

The hypothesized Run return contract does not apply. Application.Run registers context.AfterFunc(ctx,a.Close) and calls d.Run(a.ctx,a). Driver.Run returns ctx.Err only before any native window starts. After started=true and core.Wait(), it returns the recorded refresh/device/native failure if present, otherwise nil; it does not return ctx.Err on normal post-start shutdown. The smoke cancels after publishing its check result, by which point real native windows have started. Keeping err propagation preserves legitimate native/device failures. Consecutive live fixtures already exit0 on this contract; no context.Canceled suppression is needed.

The fixture injects system events by queue, not direct widget dispatch. WindowByName protects only the registry slice with AppMulti.Mu; Name/SetName are not mutex protected, and native NewWindow publishes before SetName, so startup lookup is not generally thread safe. Main fixture lookup occurs after stable actual AX geometry/actions and before it opens a second window. Workbench lookup now occurs only after its actual modal geometry/hit-test probe and owner-accepted modal edit; no other window starts during either lookup. Source.KeyChord constructs a fresh event and only calls Deque.Send under its mutex. core.renderWindow.handleEvent later dispatches under renderContext.Lock. The early post-Open lookup was removed, rather than relying on the registry lock for window-field publication.

ui.Numeric is mandatory for both Slider and NumberField. Numeric.Validate rejects nonfinite fields, Max<=Min, Step<=0, oversized span/step and values outside the declared range; ValidateControl always invokes it for both numeric kinds. There is no optional/unbounded flag. Driver refresh, control mount and Workbench Mount/Sync validate descriptors before accessibility publication, so omitted or 0..0 bounds cannot reach the native tree. Existing TestControlValidationAndFocus rejects zero Step, and TestAccessibilityNumericDescriptionsRejectNonfiniteBeforeSnapshot covers nonfinite values in all four numeric fields. A portable contract probe additionally verifies omitted/equal-zero bounds and zero Step are refused for both kinds while a declared 0..10 range is accepted. Publishing validated Min/Max is required, and suppressing those pointers would misrepresent supported controls.

Native window registry mutex only protects iteration, not Name/SetName. The fixture now obtains native handles only after stable live accessibility probes. The startup workbench lookup before that barrier was removed; production focus/event tests pass repeatedly with first raw Escape delivered once. Event enqueue itself uses Deque.Send mutex; dispatch occurs under the modal originating renderContext.

AX page handlers use the common delivery invalidation path. accessibilityDeliver posts to the registered logical window, rechecks lifetime/generation, resolves the current handler, and calls owner.Invalidate(window) whenever that handler accepts the action. This covers both VirtualTree accessibilityTreePage (returns true after updating Start) and VirtualTable SetViewport (returns true on success); neither handler needs a second local invalidation. Application.Invalidate marks the matching window dirty and wakes the driver. The Custom event handler drains accepted owner callbacks before syncTopology and refresh(w). Refresh consumes TakeDirty, validates/reconciles the descriptor, and reconcile calls syncRecord; ui.Extension syncRecord calls ext.Sync on every reconciliation, even with the same Custom pointer. VirtualTree.Sync updates its fixed native row pool and v.visible from the accepted Start; VirtualTable.Sync updates its pool from Model.View. Only afterward does refresh call syncAccessibility, which stamps current materialized domain IDs before publishing the semantic snapshot. Geometry is published after render. Both repeated final native AX runs accepted tree Next/Previous page actions, observed the recycled row with nonzero geometry, and verified the actual native pager hit-test target; the table Next page action likewise replaced row-0 with row-4. The finding overlooks this verified cross-file delivery/refresh path.
